scenes.headline: NEW TAB, *WRITTEN BY AI*
scenes.sub: An AI homepage rebuilt from your browsing
scenes.say: Okay, someone at {Anthropic|Anthropic} just built an AI homepage that literally writes itself.

scenes.heading: HOW IT *WORKS*
steps: Opens up to 8 sites you follow
scenes.say: It reads your browsing history, opens up to {8|eight} sites you follow, and then writes you a fresh front page.
And it's his own open-source project, which hit {300|three hundred} stars in just twelve hours.

scenes.heading: ANY *LOOK* YOU WANT
scenes.say: You can make it look like a morning newspaper, a dashboard, or even a green hacker terminal.

scenes.title: Terminal
scenes.heading: CHROME + *YOUR* API KEY
scenes.say: Setup is quick: you load it in Chrome with your own {Anthropic|Anthropic} {API|A P I} key.
But here's the catch: it sends your history and up to {8|eight} signed-in pages to {Anthropic|Anthropic}, and every build costs you credits. The good news? Uploads get deleted after each build.
So, would you let AI write your homepage? Comment {TAB|tab} and I'll pin the link.

AI Homepage replaces Chrome's new tab with a front page that Claude writes from your own browsing: it reads your history, opens up to 8 sites you follow and writes a fresh page in any look (newspaper, dashboard, terminal). It rebuilds itself in the background.
The catch: each build sends your history summary and up to 8 signed-in pages to the Anthropic API, and costs API credits. Uploads are deleted after each build.
Repo: github.com/ThariqS/ai-newtab (MIT). The newspaper image is the README's illustration.
